superseded_note: SECOND PASS (independent review, 2026-08-20): the 2026-08-19 implementation this contract originally certified was CRITICALLY FLAWED — REPAIR_RECHECK_EPSILON_MS=1 declared a repair 'clear' the instant it landed, because no run outcome could possibly exist yet at now()+1ms; every repair attempt in real production timing would pass trivially regardless of whether it actually fixed anything. runAutoRepairAsync is now a durable, evidence-gated state machine: one decision per call (matching one real sweep tick), never declares success/failure without sufficient REAL post-repair outcomes (the SAME D2.2 guardrail registry + DEFAULT_MIN_GUARDRAIL_SAMPLE_COUNT threshold), and truthfully accounts for non-actionable diagnoses and infra failures. See auto_repair_service.ts's module doc comment and docs/ai/runs/2026-08-19-d2-lifecycle-independent-review.md.

judgment_calls: REPLACED the flawed same-tick 'no evidence yet = success' design entirely: runAutoRepairAsync now processes exactly ONE decision per call and reads all durable state (repairAttemptCount, repairRecheckAfter, repairProposalIdsJson) fresh from the PostApplyEvent every time — it is meant to be called on every scheduler sweep tick (post_apply_lifecycle.ts's sweepPostApplyLifecycleAsync now calls it unconditionally for every tripped, non-terminal event, not just once).

Evidence sufficiency reuses the EXACT D2.2 guardrail registry (models/guardrail_registry.ts's evaluateGuardrails) and threshold (post_apply_monitor.ts's exported DEFAULT_MIN_GUARDRAIL_SAMPLE_COUNT) rather than a second, independently-tuned threshold — one definition of 'enough samples to trust,' never two that can drift apart.

Crash-safety for the config mutation + proposal creation/claim triad: every attempt is idempotency-keyed (`post-apply-repair:<proposalId>:attempt:<n>`) and the pre-mutation snapshot (including the value the attempt WILL apply) is persisted on the proposal row's before_snapshot_json BEFORE any live mutation runs — a resumed call after a crash reads that durable snapshot rather than re-deriving 'prior value' from a possibly-already-mutated live config, so it can never double-mutate the same attempt.

The config-field write now goes through a real value+revision CAS primitive (compareAndSetConfigField, shared with the revert path) instead of an unconditional AgentConfigsRepository.update() — a concurrent human/automation edit to the SAME field during the repair window is detected and refused rather than silently overwritten.

The protected-field refusal in resolveRepairConfigPatch now reuses UNSAFE_WHOLE_FIELD_SCOPE_FIELDS (org_proposal_apply.ts) — the SAME set the human apply/revert paths already enforce — instead of a bespoke single-field ('allowedSkillsJson') check, so it can never drift if that protected set ever grows.

THIRD PASS (this repair): landConfigFieldWithProjection (org_proposal_apply.ts) is the shared primitive behind issue-1433-c12 AND issue-1434-c14 (revert) — one definition of 'a config-field mutation is settled' (value CAS + profile-projection gate), reused by repair-attempt landing and revert restoration so they can never drift on what counts as a completed mutation.

THIRD PASS: resuming a durable attempt (issue-1433-c13) now happens BEFORE diagnosis unconditionally, not only after a detected crash — the dedup-key lookup runs on every 'make new attempt' entry into the state machine, so the fresh-diagnosis path is reached only when no durable row exists yet for that exact attempt number.
